title: Leaf count after path pruning
statement: Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, and let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols with inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$. Suppose a specified sequence of branch choices in $p$ leads to the subtree $s$, and $s$ has strictly fewer output leaves than $p$. Then deleting that path by splicing out the branch to $s$ yields a protocol with $\mathrm{numLeaves}(p)-\mathrm{numLeaves}(s)$ output leaves.
hypotheses_covered: Protocols $s$ and $p$ over input types $X,Y$ and output type $\alpha$
A specified subprotocol path from $s$ to $p$
replaced:
Let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols, and let $s$ lie
along a subprotocol path inside $p$, so that $s$ occurs as a rooted subtree of $p$. If
$s$ has strictly fewer leaves than $p$, that is, if the number of leaves of $s$ is less
than the number of leaves of $p$, then the protocol obtained by pruning this path from
$p$ has exactly $\text{numLeaves}(p) - \text{numLeaves}(s)$ leaves.
